sections.h2: Which selling routes make sense for an Anna homeowner?
sections.html:
Anna homeowners can sell through an agent, sell the house themselves, or take a direct cash offer, and the tradeoff is price against speed. Anna is in north central Collin County, and its population roughly doubled in five years, so many sellers are first owners of newer homes in subdivisions that still have active builders nearby.

That second fact shapes the sale. A buyer comparing your resale with a builder's model home on the same street will look closely at price, condition and any recurring assessment on the tax bill. A cash buyer skips that comparison and prices the home in its present condition.

  • An agent listing suits a clean, newer home when you can wait for a financed buyer.
  • A sale without an agent works if you are comfortable handling the contract and title paperwork.
  • A cash offer fits a quick move, an inherited house, a tenant situation or repairs you do not want to finance.

sections.h2: How fast is Anna growing, according to the Census Bureau?
sections.html:
Anna is one of the fastest-growing places in the county. The 2010 census counted 8,249 people in 2010 and 16,896 in 2020, then estimated 35,245 by mid-2025. Measured from its 2020 starting estimate, that is a gain of 105.7%.

Anna's land area is 16.45 square miles. With a young age profile, larger households and a commute above half an hour, the typical Anna buyer is a family looking for space within reach of McKinney and the Dallas job market.

Anna is on State Highway 5 and Farm Road 455, about eleven miles northeast of McKinney, and it began with the railroad. The Texas State Historical Association says the Houston and Texas Central Railway passed through in 1873, and the town was platted in 1883 with twenty residents, two stores, a steam gristmill and a Baptist church.

Anna incorporated in 1913. For most of the twentieth century it stayed small: the Handbook of Texas gives 538 residents in 1929, 855 in the mid-1980s and 904 in 1990. The accounts of how it got its name differ, with several stories tied to the railroad's officials and a local founder's family.

Anna's growth is so recent that many of its houses are young as well. Questions that come up in these sales include expired builder warranties, drainage on newly graded lots and neighborhood-level assessments.

sections.h2: Do special districts or assessments affect an Anna sale?
sections.html:
They can. Anna's City Council creates public improvement districts by resolution, and the city's public documents include Resolution 2023-02-1378, approved February 14, 2023, creating The Woods at Lindsey Place Public Improvement District. A PID lets a city finance streets, utilities and similar improvements through assessments on the lots that benefit.

Collin County also has many municipal utility districts and water districts, and Collin CAD's rate table lists them as separate taxing entities. A house in one of these districts has an extra line on the property tax bill.

  • Have the title company check whether the lot is inside a PID or a utility district.
  • Ask the Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector which entities appear on your tax statement.
  • Ask the city for the PID's assessment schedule if the lot is inside one.
  • Give the buyer those figures early so the price conversation uses the real annual cost.

sections.h2: What permits and inspections does Anna require?
sections.html:
Anna's Building Department handles permits and inspections from the Municipal Complex at 120 W. 7th Street, Suite 142, open on weekdays from eight to five The city's permit information page lists requirements for fences, irrigation, remodels, roofing, solar panels, pools and spas, water heaters and patio covers.

Inspections are requested by email by 4 p.m. on the business day before, and none are done on weekends or holidays. The city also lists extra forms that may be required, including a site drainage acknowledgement, a homeowner's affidavit and a pool affidavit.

Before listing, the useful step is to confirm that any fence, pool, roof or remodel work done during your ownership was permitted and finaled. A buyer's inspector often asks, and a missing final can stall the closing. The Building Department phone is 972-924-2616.

sections.h2: How are Anna property taxes billed and when are they due?
sections.html:
Anna's property tax bill comes from the Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector. Statements go out in October and are treated as due when received, and the county says January 31 is the date to beat for avoiding penalties. Since a lien for the year attaches on January 1, the title company will ask that any balance be paid out of your proceeds.

In the 2023 table that Collin CAD published, Anna city offered the exemptions below. The district posts a new table each year, so confirm the current entries:

  • Homestead: 3.00% of value, with a $5,000 floor.
  • Age 65 or older: $30,000.
  • Disabled person: $30,000.

If you move in partway through a year, you may be able to claim the homestead exemption for the rest of that year when the prior owner held none. Owners with an age-based or disability exemption on school taxes have a ceiling on that bill, and Collin CAD says the ceiling can follow the owner to another Texas home as a percentage.

Homestead appraisals are capped at 10% growth a year, plus new improvements. The cap limits taxable value, so a long-time owner's bill can trail the market price of the house.

sections.h2: What changes when an Anna house is inherited or facing foreclosure?
sections.html:
Collin County offices handle the filings, and the state rules are short.

  • Heirs: someone who inherited but is not on the recorded deed can still claim the homestead exemption by giving the appraisal district a sworn statement of ownership, the death certificate and a recent utility bill. The small-estate route is closed when the estate holds real property other than a homestead.
  • Lender action: a sale notice must precede the first-Tuesday auction by 21 days or more, and a borrower can cure within 20 days of the default letter.
  • Deeds: the Collin County Clerk accepts originals or certified copies that are signed and notarized.

Where time is short, a sale before the auction date lets you set the closing timeline yourself. A cash buyer has no loan approval to wait for, which can shorten the calendar.

faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 35,245 residents on July 1, 2025, more than double the 2020 estimates base of 17,137, and the city has 16.45 square miles of land.

faqs.q: Is a PID assessment passed to the buyer when I sell an Anna house?
faqs.a: Yes, an assessment attached to the lot stays with the property. Ask the title company and the city for the schedule, and share it with buyers up front.

faqs.q: Which county office collects tax for Anna?
faqs.a: The Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector bills and collects it. Collin Central Appraisal District, in McKinney, sets the value and processes exemptions.

faqs.q: Should I gather permit records before listing in Anna?
faqs.a: It is not a statutory step, but buyers and inspectors ask for it. Anna's Building Department can tell you which permits were issued and whether they were finaled.

faqs.q: Can an heir claim the homestead exemption on an inherited Anna house?
faqs.a: Yes. Heirs not named on a recorded deed file an affidavit of ownership interest with the appraisal district, along with the death certificate and a recent utility bill.
